title: Photosynthesis
standard_text: The process of photosynthesis: the word and balanced equations; the light phase and the dark phase (Calvin cycle); the role of chlorophyll, light, carbon dioxide and water; limiting factors (light intensity, CO₂ concentration and temperature); greenhouses; investigations of photosynthesis. (summary of the senior secondary Biology curriculum, SSS 1; WAEC and NECO syllabuses)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 Biology worksheets (senior secondary curriculum, WAEC and NECO): photosynthesis, photosynthesis in leaves, early experiments and pigments, the light phase and the dark phase and limiting factors. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The oxygen released comes from water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplasts. In the light phase (in the grana), light energy splits water into hydrogen and oxygen; oxygen is released and energy is stored in ATP. In the dark phase (in the stroma), carbon dioxide is combined with hydrogen to form glucose.

The rate of photosynthesis is limited by whichever factor is in shortest supply: light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration or temperature. Farmers use greenhouses to control these factors. Starch tests and the bubbles from pondweed are used to investigate photosynthesis.

Example

Which gas is released in photosynthesis?

It comes from water.

Answer: oxygen

Example

Light is increased but the rate stays the same. Why?

Another factor is limiting.

Answer: CO₂ or temperature is now limiting

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking the oxygen comes from CO₂.
  • Thinking the dark phase only happens at night.

faq.q: Why are leaves destarched before a starch test?
faq.a: So that any starch found must have been made during the experiment.

faq.q: Why is photosynthesis important for all life?
faq.a: It produces food (glucose) and oxygen and removes carbon dioxide from the air.

items.q: What is a limiting factor?
c: the factor that is in shortest supply and so controls the rate
the temperature at which an enzyme denatures
the factor that is present in excess
a factor that stops a reaction for ever
items.e: Light, CO₂ and temperature limit photosynthesis.

items.q: Where does the Calvin cycle (light-independent reaction) take place?
items.e: It uses ATP and reduced NADP.

items.q: What is the name for the enzyme that fixes CO₂ onto RuBP?

items.q: Which photosystem is used in cyclic photophosphorylation?

items.q: A competitive inhibitor slows an enzyme. How does it work?

sets.title: The dark phase and limiting factors

items.q: Which stage of photosynthesis? ATP and NADPH are used to build glucose.
items.e: Light reactions make ATP/NADPH; the Calvin cycle uses them.

items.q: A lamp is 30 cm from a pondweed. It is moved to 10 cm. What happens to the light intensity?
items.e: Light intensity ∝ 1/distance². 1/3 of the distance → 3² times.

items.q: Which process is this? carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen
items.e: Match the reactants and products.

items.q: What are the products of anaerobic respiration in muscles?
items.e: Anaerobic respiration in muscles: glucose → lactic acid.
